name: Wang Ning
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2021-2024); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026); Hurun Global U40 (2021-2026); Hurun China U40 (2021-2022); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Ning is the founder, chairman and CEO of Hong Kong-listed toy maker Pop Mart International Group.
Set up in 2010, it sells small figurines and plush toys in so-called blind box packaging that doesn't reveal the exact toys inside.
Pop Mart's Labubu line of dolls once ignited a global collection craze over the rabbit-ish creature that has jagged teeth and a mischievous grin.
The company has launched Labubu-themed jewelry and bakery brands as it seeks additional revenue streams. It has also built a theme park named Pop Land in Beijing.
forbes_facts: Labubu was created by Hong Kong-born artist Kasing Lung. It has been collected by celebrities including Dua Lipa, Rihanna and Blackpink's Lisa.

name: Denise York
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2017)
forbes_bio: Denise York's family owns more than 90% of the San Francisco 49ers, the NFL's sixth-most valuable team and the 2023 Super Bowl runner-up.
York's father, Edward DeBartolo Sr. (d. 1994), bought the team for $13 million in 1977. It is now worth more than $8 billion.
York took control of the 49ers in 2000 from her brother, Edward Jr., who found himself in legal trouble after owning the team for 23 years.
Denise and her husband John have four children, the oldest of whom, Jed, serves as the current CEO of the 49ers.
Her husband John, a pathologist, founded DeYor Laboratories in Youngstown, Ohio before selling it to Corning.
York and her family finalized their takeover of English soccer club Leeds United in 2023. They paid more than $200 million to acquire the remaining 56% stake.
forbes_facts: York's first job after college was building the HR department of the family's company.
York's father was also an owner of NHL's Pittsburgh Penguins. Denise was the team's president in 1991 when it won its first-ever Stanley Cup.

name: Marie-Hélène Habert-Dassault
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Marie-Hélène Habert-Dassault is an heir to the Dassault aerospace and software fortune, which she inherited along with her siblings when her father Serge Dassault died in 2018.
Habert was the president of the supervisory board of family-controlled aerospace and software conglomerate Dassault Groupe, but stepped down in 2019.
She now serves as the conglomerate's Communication and Partnership director.
Marcel, Habert's grandfather, founded Dassault Aviation, a French aerospace company that started out making propellers in World War I.
The Dassaults also own the country's daily newspaper Le Figaro, vineyards and a private aeronautic company.

name: Wei Jianjun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2003-2026)
forbes_bio: Wei Jianjun is the chairman of Great Wall Motor, one of China's largest SUV manufacturers, which sells to over 170 countries and regions.
He took over the debt-plagued Great Wall Automobile Industry Company, the predecessor to the current business, in 1990 when he was only 26.
Wei worked at a carpet factory and a water-pump factory before joining Great Wall.
Great Wall started up its first Brazil plant in August 2025. It is part of the company's 10 billion reais ($1.9 billion) planned investment in the country.

name: Arnon Milchan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2004-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Arnon Milchan owns film and TV production company New Regency Enterprises.
New Regency has produced hits like Pretty Woman, Mr. and Mrs. Smith, The Revenant, Birdman and Bohemian Rhapsody.
Milchan transformed his family's bankrupt fertilizer company, which he took over in 1962 at the age of 21, into a $125 million business.
He was a business student, professional soccer player and consultant for weapons systems between Israeli Defense Forces and U.S. defense contractors.
Milchan has been ensnared in the corruption probe into Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyanhu, but will reportedly not be charged with wrongdoing.
forbes_facts: An avid art collector, Milchan also paints his own paintings.

name: Matthias Reinhart
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Matthias Reinhart is chairman and majority shareholder of VZ Holding Ltd., a Swiss financial services company he took public in 2007.
After getting his MBA at University of St. Gallen, he worked at McKinsey & Co. in Zurich and Chicago before co-founding VZ in 1993.
VZ's key proposition: bringing transparency to a market that made it hard for customers to compare the prices and benefits of financial products.
The firm does not broker financial products; instead, customers pay a fee for advisory and portfolio-management services.
forbes_facts: Reinhart is a member of the advisory board of NZZ (Neue Zuercher Zeitung), a Swiss, German-language daily newspaper.
He also sits on the founding board of the Swiss Epilepsy Foundation.

name: Rajiv Bajaj
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2023-2025); Hurun India (2019)
forbes_bio: Rajiv Bajaj is the son of the late Rahul Bajaj, who was chairman emeritus of the storied Bajaj Group until his death in February 2022.
The group was founded by his great-grandfather Jamnalal Bajaj, who set it up in 1926 and was a follower of Mahatma Gandhi.
Today, the Bajaj Group is a conglomerate of 40 companies in sectors such as two-wheelers, financial services and electrical appliances.
Rajiv runs two-wheeler flagship Bajaj Auto.
In 2025, the family agreed to buy out Germant giant Allianz's stake In their two insurance joint ventures for $2.8 billion.
forbes_facts: Rajiv is passionate about yoga and homeopathy.
His younger brother Sanjiv is also a billionaire.

name: Hamad bin Jassim bin Jaber Al Thani
name_chinese: 哈马德·本·贾西姆·本·贾伯·塔尼
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026)
forbes_bio: Hamad bin Jassim Al Thani was prime minister of Qatar between 2007 and 2013; he also served as foreign minister from 1992 until 2013.
His great uncle founded modern Qatar in 1971, and he's a cousin of the current Emir.
Through an entity called Paramount Services Holdings, Al Thani owns 4.5% of Deustche Bank, his biggest publicly-traded holding.
In 2016, he was mentioned in the "Panama Papers"--leaked files from Panama law firm Mossack Fonseca, which set up offshore entities for clients.
forbes_facts: Al Thani, known as HBJ, has a 436-foot superyacht, called Al Mirqab, worth an estimated $300 million, according to the Panama Papers.
He served as Qatar's spokesman in the U.S., making the rounds of talk shows in 2017 to defend his country against Saudi Arabia's charges that it supports terrorism.

name: Nusli Wadia
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Nusli Wadia is chairman of the Wadia Group, a cookies-to-textiles empire with roots in shipbuilding dating back to 1736.
Group companies include Britannia Industries and home textiles company Bombay Dyeing.
His loss-making budget airline, Go First, declared bankruptcy in 2023.
Wadia is often referred to as a corporate samurai by the Indian press for waging numerous legal battles.
One notable battle was against the Tata Group and his former pal Ratan Tata, who got him ousted from the boards of three Tata firms in 2016.
forbes_facts: Wadia is the grandson of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, founder of Pakistan.
Wadia's son Ness co-owns Indian Premier League cricket team Kings XI Punjab.
In September 2024 Nusli Wadia sold a 10-acre parcel in Mumbai for over $130 million.

name: Scott Shleifer
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Scott Shleifer cofounded Tiger Global Management's private equity investing arm in 2003, two years after Chase Coleman founded the hedge fund firm.
Tiger Global's venture funds now make up the bulk of the firm's $50 billion in net assets under management.
Shleifer made lucrative bets on several Chinese tech companies for Tiger, including JD.com, ride-hailing app Didi Chuxing and e-commerce giant Meituan.
Shleifer stepped down as Tiger Global's head of private equity at the start of 2024, transitioning to a role as senior advisor.
He bought a 21,000-square-foot Palm Beach mansion in 2021 for $123 million.
